lesson_title: Two Friends, One Till: the Partnership Year, Revised
hook_text: Every partnership fight is one of two sentences. Accounting answers both.
clip_script: Two friends open a shop. One puts in more money. The other works longer hours. Within a month, the dangerous sentences arrive: 'I put in more, so more is mine.' 'I work harder, so more is mine.' Every partnership fight in history is one of those two — and the partnership agreement answers both before the shouting: a salary for the one who works, interest for the money that waits, a ratio for whatever remains. Watch it run. The year's pot: two hundred and forty thousand rand. Ladle one — wages for work: ninety-six and seventy-two. Ladle two — thanks to the waiting money: twenty and ten. Ladle three — the promised bonus: twelve. What's left? Thirty thousand — split as agreed, fifteen each. Count the plates: one thirty-one plus one-oh-nine — exactly two hundred and forty. The pot empties to the rand, and that emptiness is the proof: appropriation never creates or loses a cent. It only divides — fairly, on paper, with the friendship intact.
visual_style: Two friends at one till; a glowing profit pot emptied by four labelled ladles onto two plates; the plates weighing exactly against the pot; a signed agreement page glowing beneath everything.
mood: Warm but precise — fairness as arithmetic.
pacing: Conflict setup, four ladle beats, the empty-pot proof landing last.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and divide the pot yourself.
